title: Ephemeral session heartbeat and connection recycle guidance across SDKs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: customer apps experience intermittent streaming stalls and slow first-byte latencies after long idle periods. Root cause signals point to a combination of: (1) OS-level TCP ephemeral port exhaustion from long-lived half-closed sockets; (2) stale connections in language runtimes not being recycled aggressively enough; (3) mismatch between client keepalive defaults and server-side ALB/NGINX idle timeouts. Goal: provide a cross-SDK reference cookbook (Python/TypeScript/Go) with recommended defaults, rationale, and minimal code examples; plus implement opt-in automatic session heartbeat and connection-recycle helper utilities in each SDK.
background: We see production incidents (internal postmortem linked) where long-tail clients (mobile, serverless) hold connections and then attempt streaming requests that block. Existing guidance scattered across tickets (e.g., ENG-32901) is inconsistent between languages. This ticket standardizes: heartbeat interval, max idle lifetime for pooled connections, pool sizing heuristics, and streaming reconnect/backoff rules.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Publish cross-language cookbook doc in repo + Confluence. 2) SDKs ship the helper: `SessionHeartbeat` (Python/TS/Go) that defaults to enabling a lightweight keepalive ping on streaming sessions and triggers connection pool recycle after N misses. 3) Unit + integration tests covering long-idle reuse and graceful reconnect on server-initiated close. 4) Benchmarks demonstrating no regression in P50 latency and <10% token-cost delta under typical workloads.
technical_decisions: 1) Heartbeat will be an application-level noop frame (not HTTP-level) where possible to avoid ALB influence; fall back to TCP keepalive if transport doesn’t support it. 2) Default heartbeat interval: 30s. Rationale: balances ALB idle defaults (60s) and mobile battery considerations. 3) Connection recycle: enforce IdleConnTimeout=2x heartbeat (60s) in SDK-managed transports. 4) Streaming ergonomics: implement idempotent reconnect with exponential backoff + jitter; preserve partial KV cache where feasible; expose a `resume_token` parameter for long running sessions.
language_guidance_examples: Python (aiohttp): use TCPConnector(limit=100, keepalive_timeout=60) and a background asyncio.Task that sends application-level ping frames every 30s. Example: connector = TCPConnector(limit=100, keepalive_timeout=60); agent = ClientSession(connector=connector)

TypeScript (Node): new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 200, keepAliveMsecs: 30000, timeout: 120000 }) ; pass agent into fetch/axios. Add lightweight newline-delimited ping over streaming SSE/WebSocket where available.

Streaming resume: SDKs will accept an optional `resume_token` and call `client.stream({resume_token})` after reconnect to continue. If underlying model runtime supports KV cache resumption, surface hook `on_resume(kv_delta)` to rehydrate local caches.
tradeoffs:
- Shorter heartbeat reduces stale-socket risk but increases client CPU/wake-ups on battery constrained devices. We default to 30s but make it configurable.
- Application-level pings add protocol complexity; TCP keepalives are simpler but often bypassed by proxies/load-balancers. We implement layered approach: app-level ping preferred, TCP keepalive fallback.
- Aggressive pool recycling reduces long-tail failures but can increase connection churn and TLS handshakes; we recommend conservative defaults and provide templates for high-throughput customers to tune towards fewer reconnects.
tests_and_benchmarks: Spike results: ran 6hr soak with 10k simulated clients; default Node agent keptAlive + IdleConnTimeout=120s exhibited 2.3x increase in ephemeral port usage vs tuned settings. After applying heartbeat(30s)+IdleConnTimeout=60s we observed 0.9x baseline ephemeral port usage and eliminated streaming stalls in 95th percentile. Added unit tests for connection-recycle hook and integration test simulating server-initiated FIN. See benchmark artifact: https://internal-artifacts.redwood.ai/benchmarks/ENG-91247/soak-2026-03-02.html
implementation_notes: Work split: (A) Python SDK change: add `SessionHeartbeat` helper + extend `ClientSession` factory; (B) TS SDK: add AgentFactory + `enableSessionHeartbeat` boolean; (C) Go SDK: export `TransportPool` helper with `HeartbeatInterval` and `RecycleAfter` fields. Each change gated behind minor SDK bump and runtime-2026.03 release tag. Ensure feature flags for customers to opt-out.
risks:
- Misconfiguration could increase TLS handshake cost for small deployments. Mitigation: document cost tradeoffs and provide recommended profiles for interactive vs high-throughput workloads.
- In some environments (strict corporate proxies) app-level heartbeats may be dropped; fallback path must be robust.
